Compare reinsurance programmes

Source: R/programmes.R
compare_reinsurance.Rd

Simulates the claims of a portfolio once and puts them through each of several reinsurance programmes (a quota share, an excess of loss layer on each claim and an aggregate stop loss, alone or together), to compare what each costs with the capital it saves: the expected ceded losses, the reinsurance premiums, the margin paid to the reinsurers, the net result, its value at risk and the capital it needs.

Usage

compare_reinsurance(
  frequency,
  frequency_params,
  severity,
  severity_params,
  programmes,
  premium,
  n = 10000,
  level = 0.995,
  loading = 0.25,
  coc_rate = 0.1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

frequency, frequency_params

The claim count distribution and its parameters, as in simulate_claims, such as "Poisson" (lambda) or "Negative Binomial" (r, beta).

severity, severity_params

The claim size distribution and its parameters, as in simulate_claims, such as "LogNormal" (meanlog, sdlog) or "Pareto" (alpha, x_m).

programmes

A named list of programmes, each a list with any of: quota_share (the share ceded) and commission (the ceding commission, a share of the ceded premium); xl, a list with the deductible, limit, reinstatements (Inf, the default, for unlimited and free), reinstatement_rate (1 by default) and optionally premium; and stop_loss, a list with the attachment, limit and optionally premium. "No reinsurance" is added as the first programme.

premium

The subject premium of the year.

n

The number of simulated years.

level

The level of the value at risk, such as 0.995.

loading

The share of a priced layer's or stop loss's premium for the reinsurer's expenses and profit.

coc_rate

The cost of capital a year, for the value of the capital relief.

seed

A whole number for a reproducible run, or NULL. The stream of the R session is restored after a run with a seed.

Value

An object of class netsimr_programmes, a list with summary, a data frame with a row per programme (the expected ceded loss, the reinsurance premium and margin, the net mean result and its standard deviation, the probability of a loss-making year, the value at risk of the net result, the capital, the capital relief and its value), results, the simulated net result of each programme (a column each), and the settings.

Details

Every programme sees the same simulated claims. In each, the quota share cedes its share of every claim first; the excess of loss layer then recovers from each retained claim the part above its deductible, up to its limit, and at most \((1 + \textrm{reinstatements})\) limits a year; the stop loss last recovers the part of the year's retained claims above its attachment, up to its limit.

The premium of a quota share is its share of the subject premium, less its ceding commission. A layer's or stop loss's premium is given or, when it is not, priced at the expected ceded loss with loading as the share of the premium for the reinsurer's expenses and profit (technical_premium, with the reinstatements the simulations use). The excess of loss layer's reinstatement premiums are paid pro rata to the cover reinstated.

The net result of a year is the subject premium less the reinsurance premiums paid, plus the ceding commission, less the retained claims (before other expenses). The capital a programme needs is the mean net result less its \(1 - \textrm{level}\) quantile: what a bad year at that level costs against an average one. The capital relief is the capital without reinsurance less the programme's, and its value is coc_rate of the relief less the margin paid for it: positive when the programme saves more in the cost of capital than it costs.

See also

simulate_claims, technical_premium and run_shiny_reinsurance_pricing_tool, which compares programmes on its Programmes tab.

Examples

programmes <- list(
  `Quota share 30%` = list(quota_share = 0.3, commission = 0.25),
  `XL 4m xs 1m` = list(xl = list(deductible = 1e6, limit = 4e6, reinstatements = 1)),
  `Stop loss 30m xs 45m` = list(stop_loss = list(attachment = 45e6, limit = 30e6))
)
cmp <- compare_reinsurance("Poisson", 200, "LogNormal", c(11, 1.5), programmes,
                           premium = 60e6, n = 5000, seed = 1)
cmp
#> Reinsurance programmes, 5,000 simulated years, capital at 99.5%

#>  Stop loss 30m xs 45m    785,492   261,831  22,904,382  8,951,704 21,080,989
#>       value
